I primarily used the climbing gym, yoga program, and occasionally attended Muay Thai classes. Unfortunately, over the years I watched membership costs increase significantly while staffing levels, programming, and amenities declined.

My biggest concern is the climbing program. Reduced staffing appeared to coincide with a decline in supervision and training opportunities. During my membership, there were incidents involving members failing to properly clip into auto-belays, resulting in serious falls and injuries. At the same time, classes and instruction that helped educate climbers were reduced or eliminated.

I raised these concerns directly with management. My emails to the General Manager went unanswered, while the Regional Manager responded and indicated that member feedback could help influence decisions regarding staffing and operating hours. In an effort to gather constructive feedback from other members, I created a Google form. Shortly afterward, my membership was terminated. When I asked for a clear explanation of what I had done wrong, none was provided, which left me feeling that the termination was retaliatory.

What is most disappointing is that the climbing community at Chelsea Piers was once one of its greatest strengths. Instead of investing in that community, management appears to have prioritized cost-cutting measures that reduced services and member engagement.

There are now competing facilities that offer lower prices, longer climbing hours, stronger instruction programs, and a greater emphasis on safety. The gym does not feel cramped or claustrophobic. The natural light helps me feel more energized and positive. The equipment is state-of-the-art and always in good condition, and you can choose from a variety of weight-lifting and cardio machines.

The staff is friendly and helpful, and the goers are respectful and friendly. Another thing I appreciate about Mercedes Club is that it respects my privacy and personal space. I am the person that likes to be left alone to work out and that is possible there. The staff and the goers are not intrusive or pushy, and they let me do my own thing. I can focus on my goals and enjoy my time at the gym. The ambiance is nice and motivating, without being too noisy or distracting.

The club is also equipped with an indoor and outdoor pool which is a great bonus. The outdoor pool is especially nice in the summer when I can enjoy the sun and the breeze.

The only thing that could be an annoyance is the peak hours on weekdays when the gym gets busy between 6 and 8 pm like any other club in NY. But even then, the gym is large enough to fit everyone comfortably, and you can always find a place to do your workout.

I enjoy going there and I think you will too. It's the perfect place for anyone who wants to take care of their health and fitness. The club is also equipped with an indoor and outdoor pool which is a great bonus. The outdoor pool is especially nice in the summer when I can enjoy the sun and the breeze.

Instead the club focuses on upselling you on things like $12 smoothies and $150+ spa treatments.

---

Pros:
+ Pretty good hours (late nights and weekends). Though the showers close 30min before the publicized hours so if you actually stay late you'll be forced to shower at home.
+ A lot of squat racks (~8+)
+ Equipment itself is high quality and there are a full range of machines.
+ Large footprint (square footage)
+ Good variety of exercise classes included
+ Mobile App is solid compared to most gyms
+ Good location
+ Staff is very friendly (though limited) and available to answer questions which is great. Other gyms don't answer the phone.
+ Not really crowded (at least on weekends and late evenings so I haven't experienced waiting for equipment)
+ Rainfall showers, sauna, hot tub are nice.

Cons:
- Trash:  Way too much trash strewn about. e.g Men's locker room bins overflowing, small scraps of paper, gum wrappers,  used chap stick left behind, razor blade caps (left in showers), clothing tags, etc. I've reported this to the management on at least 2 occasions with no improvement. Part of this is on the guests/members for not being as considerate but regardless of fault it impacts the experience really negatively. This is especially in my experience closer to the end of the day, which feels understaffed.  Uploaded some photos (but it's so common you can just come for a tour late evening tomorrow and you'll see it for yourself). I just heard another member this morning complaining in the locker room about "how frustrating it is to see people lift heavy weights then not able to lift the towels or trash to the receptacles."
- Poor maintenance:   Towels consistently overflowing the bins, strewn about in locker room benches. Non-reserved lockers aren't cleared out every night but only a few times/week (as told to me by the staff) which limits locker availability. The outside shower floors don't seem to properly drain excess water.  In the lobby of the club, where I sit as I write this, the tables are wobbly and there's left behind bottle cap and straw wrapper on the table next to me from before I sat down. 1 of 3 flat bench press stations was misaligned so that the heavier plates were inaccessible (this was fixed after reported to staff but to my main point is an indicator of low focus on basic details with guest experience)
- Few cable pull machines (<5)
- It's all underground (in an old bank vault type space) which means although the square footage is technically high, the individual spaces with many narrow maze like hallways you feel a little cramped and closed in. Plus it blocks my cell phone reception.

Small bits of feedback to management:
- The mobile app "schedule" section doesn't allow you to save a favorited filter as the default so, although it does save my class filters as a favorited group, I have to reselect the same filter (2 annoying extra steps) every time I want to see the classes without all the daycare stuff mixed in.
- The website pricing was broken when trying to signup for 3 member bundle  the advertised price showed "adults" but then going through checkout  it requires that 1 member must be a dependent.
- Would be nice to have face wash in the locker rooms, not just hand soap.
- At the risk of worsening the trash issue, I think it would be nice to have floss-picks available in the locker room. (Ideally the compostable ones to reduce waste)

In conclusion, the club offers more than a more affordable gym but it doesn't feel like your getting a great value given the service. It's 3.5x the price of my last gym at ~20% better quality offering in my opinion. If we take 5 stars as the ideal gym, the first half-star comes off for the broken showers. There are only four showers in the men’s locker room, and two of them are broken. In one of them, even the light no longer works. In my opinion, that is simply not serious.

I am also taking off one full star for the way the space is organized. For those who do not know, this gym has two floors: the first floor is a bit smaller, and the second floor is a bit bigger. The issue is that there is an unreasonable number of cardio machines. There is already a large cardio area on the second floor, but for some reason, half of the first floor is also taken up by cardio equipment.

To be clear, even during peak hours on a Monday evening, the upstairs cardio area is not completely full. The downstairs cardio area is almost never busy - usually there are just a couple of people there.

This could be fixed in a very simple way: either remove the cardio area from the first floor completely and replace it with a proper stretching area, a free weights area, kettlebells, and similar equipment, or reduce the upstairs cardio area and use that space for free weights instead.

The final half-star comes off for the free weights area. Honestly, it is not serious. This is probably the most popular area in the entire gym, yet it is squeezed into a small cramped room where it is difficult to even breathe properly. Because of that, it is constantly hot and the air feels stale. I really do not understand why this area is so poorly arranged.

To summarize: I am giving this gym 3 stars specifically because the space is badly organized. At the same time, I understand that my preferences may be specific, and maybe for the average gym user this amount of cardio equipment is fine. So objectively, the gym is probably closer to a 4. But for me personally, because of the poor layout and the free weights area, it is a 3.

UPDATE:
As of today, 3 out of 4 showers are not working - only one shower is usable.

I also would not put much trust in the owner’s response saying that repairs are supposedly planned. [{"Name":"Bunker Blake","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjV0KqL08NtbdFuSxGHzHJtby8pXF4iZSG8DWaajOm_p5bJYzsfP=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"I first started training at Hanson Fitness in 2010 when they were still on Greene Street. I was working a demanding finance job in Midtown and trying to reclaim the athleticism I’d lost after years of focusing on school, my career, and a healthy amount of partying.

At the time, I was already running and taking cycling classes, but I realized I needed to learn proper strength training. I used part of my first meaningful bonus to hire a trainer and ended up becoming a client for roughly a decade.

My first trainer was Eric K., and over the years I also worked with Clive M., Omar V., Eric E., Kirk F., Eugene, Hank, and Liz. Every trainer was different, but all were knowledgeable, professional, and genuinely enjoyable to be around. There were others I worked with episodically over the years, and while I can’t remember every name after all this time, I remember appreciating what each of them brought to the experience.

Harry Hanson deserves special recognition. Despite operating multiple studios downtown, he remained remarkably hands-on. He knew his clients, knew his trainers, and showed up. In an industry full of trends and constant reinvention, Hanson Fitness remained independent and owner-operated for more than three decades, which I find deeply admirable.

Equally important was the gym’s commitment to education. Harry built and ran a formal trainer development program, creating a culture in which coaching and learning were taken seriously. It gave the gym a different energy than most transactional fitness businesses.

When Hanson later moved to its current location, it felt like a meaningful milestone. The new space was a clear upgrade and a sign that the business had real momentum. For longtime clients, it felt less like a relocation and more like validation of everything Harry and his team had been building for years.

For me, Hanson became the foundation underneath everything else I did. During the same period, I took more than 1,000 group fitness classes, ran marathons, and played hockey at Chelsea Piers. Hanson was where I built the strength, mobility, and durability that supported it all. The stronger legs, shoulders, back, and glutes I developed there paid dividends for years.

Convenience was another major advantage. The location was ideal for anyone living below Washington Square Park. My sessions started at 6:00 a.m., and some of my favorite memories are of arriving while the city was still asleep. Before the emails, meetings, and deadlines began, a handful of people quietly prepared for the day ahead.

What stands out most in retrospect is the mix of people. This is SoHo, and personal training isn’t cheap, but Hanson somehow maintained a welcoming, grounded atmosphere. There were young professionals, retirees, entrepreneurs, executives, and people from every imaginable background all training together.

Looking back, Hanson felt like part of the invisible backbone of New York. Many people there were doing demanding work across finance, law, healthcare, technology, media, and entrepreneurship. At six in the morning, titles and money didn’t matter much. Everyone was just trying to get stronger, feel better, manage stress, and keep going. When I was younger, I assumed places like Hanson were common. With time, I realized they’re not. Hanson somehow humanized a city that is far more fragmented and isolating than it first appears. It brought together people from different industries, generations, and walks of life who otherwise might never have known one another.

Fitness is a vain, fickle, and trend-driven business. Through all of that, Hanson remained focused on the fundamentals: coaching people effectively, helping them get stronger physically and mentally, and building a sustainable business. The fact that it has endured for more than three decades in New York is not an accident.

Fifteen years later, I still use lessons I learned there. Bottom line: I do not recommend this gym to anyone who is serious about achieving results. If you don’t care, and your only priority is paying the lowest possible membership fee - then, as they say, welcome.

P.S. And this is me not even going into the fact that people have been getting their belongings stolen in the locker room more and more often. I primarily attend the women’s strength classes, and I occasionally take some of the other offerings like co-ed strength + conditioning and restore classes. Even though I had lifted before, I was intimidated to come to my first class. Tight-knit women’s fitness communities can either be incredibly welcoming or feel very cliquey, and Grassroots was such a breath of fresh air from the very beginning.

The community is warm, supportive, and genuinely encouraging - not cliquey at all. Seasoned members are always helping newer members learn the ropes, and everyone really does cheer each other on. It is the kind of place where people notice your progress and celebrate your wins.

The coaches are somehow able to balance teaching new members while still challenging seasoned members, without making anyone feel held back or left behind. There is clearly a science and method to their magic, but they make it look effortless. I can promise you there is so much thought that goes into the workout formula for every class.

What really sets Grassroots apart is how intentional they are about teaching proper form, technique, and the “why” behind each movement. The 6-week “off-the-bar” series is a perfect example — it is designed to build the skills and body awareness needed to perform better during the 8-week “on-the-bar” series. Instead of just pushing you to sweat or lift heavier, the coaches help you understand what each movement is doing, what you should be focusing on, and how to move in a way that supports your body.

I had gone to a different lifting gym years ago and often felt like I was constantly getting injured or chasing a good workout without really understanding my body. Grassroots has been completely different. I feel stronger, more confident, and much more connected to how my body works.

And on top of all of that, it is genuinely fun. The space is beautiful, the equipment is top-notch, the music is great, the teachers bring such good energy, and even the swag is fun. It feels like a place you actually want to show up to, not a place you have to drag yourself to.

They also offer resources like InBody scans, and they take the time to walk you through what every part of the scan means — not just the number on the scale. That level of education and support has helped me feel like I’m finally taking my power back.

Grassroots is more than just a gym. Over that time, it’s really helped me stay consistent and build a solid workout routine.

In terms of equipment, Synergy is very well-rounded and has everything you need regardless of your experience level. There’s a great selection of free weights and dumbbells, a dedicated deadlifting area, and a variety of machines including a Smith machine, a hip thrust machine, and plenty of options for both upper and lower body workouts as well as cardio. It’s a really versatile space whether you’re just getting started or have been training for a while.

One of the standout things about Synergy is the sense of community. The owner, Ray, is incredibly friendly and genuinely cares about the members. He goes out of his way to create a welcoming environment, and that attitude carries over to the entire staff. Everyone is approachable, chatty, and supportive, it truly starts to feel like a second family the longer you’re there. Being a member for two years really speaks to how comfortable and motivating the environment is.

Another big plus is the value. Compared to other gyms in the area, you really get a lot more for what you pay. Between the quality equipment, the welcoming atmosphere, and the supportive staff, it’s definitely worth the membership.

Not only am I now flying pain-free, but my strength, stability, and body awareness have improved so much that I can comfortably train on the trapeze three days in a row and still feel strong. My flying has noticeably improved, and I feel more capable and confident every time I step onto the rig.

What I love most is that Liberated Fitness focuses on what actually matters. You don't have to pay for fancy locker rooms, expensive weight machines, or overpriced memberships. They have everything you truly need to build a strong, resilient body that feels good to live in.

They take a holistic approach to fitness, helping you move better, prevent injuries, and become stronger in ways that translate to everyday life and whatever sport or activity you love.

[{"Name":"Sebastian C","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocJDAugtSv6swQr09CXp5tI0evdBc8oiuMeNqsBS_I-1wV-sIA=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"I have been lucky enough to train in gyms across several cities and countries because I genuinely enjoy experiencing new places through their fitness communities. Years ago, friends in New York introduced me to TMPL Hell’s Kitchen, and it has remained one of the most memorable gyms I have trained in.

The atmosphere reminds me of other lively, LGBTQIA+ friendly spaces where people are there to work hard, enjoy themselves, and make everyone feel welcome. The lighting is fun without feeling gimmicky, the equipment is clean and well maintained, and the entire gym has an energy that makes it easy to look forward to your next workout.

I have spent enough time around gyms and coaches over the years to appreciate the difference between someone who simply works as a trainer and someone who genuinely understands fitness. Before starting at X93 almost 3 years ago I was told that I needed a full knee replacement surgery. My knees were locking, unstable, and limiting what I could do day-to-day. Chris took the time to understand my specific challenges and designed a strength program that safely rebuilt the muscles supporting my knees. Over time, my pain decreased, my stability improved, and I regained confidence in my movement. Thanks to his expertise and careful coaching, I’ve been able to avoid knee replacement surgery — something I honestly didn’t think would be possible.

Beyond my knees, my overall body strength has increased dramatically. I’m stronger, and more balanced. Chris emphasizes proper form, functional strength, and sustainable progress. Every workout is intentional, challenging, and tailored to help you improve safely.

The true proof of how effective this training has been came recently when I had a fall coming down the steps of an airplane overseas. It was one of those moments that could have easily resulted in a serious injury. Instead, I was able to catch myself and walk away with only stitches on my leg. In that moment, I realized just how much strength training has protected me. The stability, muscle strength, and body awareness I’ve developed at X93 made all the difference.

Chris is knowledgeable, encouraging, and genuinely invested in his clients..The gym is immaculately clean and he and Anthony have succeeded in attracting a friendly and diverse clientele who help make the often dreaded and hard workout much less painful.

To get the workout review out of the way--yes, they are AMAZING!  I am challenged in every class, and it only makes me want to come back for more.  The coaches do a great job of programming creative workouts and are super encouraging and positive.  They very approachable, will work with you on your goals, and push you to your best in every class. Even after years of going to classes, I continue to see myself growing and improving.

However, even more important than the workouts is the Trooper mentality and community itself.  There are so many gyms and boutique fitness studios in the City, finding a place to just workout is easy.  Trooper Fitness offers something unique in the diverse and tight-knit, but welcoming, community it has built.  From encouraging each other in classes, to hanging out in the lobby afterwards, to getting together outside the gym, Trooper really is a second family to me and I have made my closest friendships in NY from people I have met at Trooper.

Their motto "All We Know is Go" really sums up their mentality.  Even in the adversity of the pandemic, the founders and coaches were on the ball in moving over to virtual workouts, and have done a great job keeping the same sense of community.
